title: Cosmopolitics 2026
summary: Leading California Forward with California State Treasurer Fiona Ma, keynote remarks and a live question-and-answer conversation

image.alt: Cosmopolitics: Leading California Forward with Fiona Ma, California State Treasurer. September 19, 2026, 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM, Mar Monte Hotel, Santa Barbara

hero.heading: The Day, Unfolded
hero.subheading: A room full of conversation, connection and community

sections.heading: Then the room began to fill

children.text: The day moved quickly from arrivals to greetings, introductions and conversation —
new faces, longtime friends, members, guests and community leaders
filling the room together
Cosmopolitics 2026 brought our community together around
public leadership, fiscal stewardship, opportunity and California’s future
For SBWPC, the afternoon also reflected a larger purpose — turning feminist values into participation, leadership and action, and expanding women’s access, voice and power

title: Run Like a Woman
summary: Run Like a Woman 2026 was an SBWPC candidate workshop focused on message, media and campaign finance

image.alt: Run Like a Woman. Message. Media. Money. The strategy. The skills. The edge to win.

hero.heading: Building the skills behind a credible campaign
hero.subheading: The strategy · The skills · The edge to win
hero.body: Run Like a Woman brought together women preparing to run for office, considering public leadership or strengthening the skills needed to compete with confidence

image.alt: Run Like a Woman. Message. Media. Money. The strategy. The skills. The edge to win.

sections.heading: Three essentials for stronger campaigns
sections.intro: The workshop focused on practical skills candidates can use immediately and continue strengthening throughout a campaign

cards.title: Fundraise with purpose
cards.body:
Connect fundraising goals to campaign strategy, relationships and the discipline of making the ask

Build a clearer finance plan and define concrete next steps

cards.title: Communicate with confidence
cards.body:
Prepare for interviews, public visibility, digital communication and the pressure of staying on message

Strengthen preparation and create a more consistent public presence

cards.title: Say why you are running
cards.body:
Turn experience, values and public purpose into language voters can understand, remember and repeat

Leave with a sharper candidate statement and clearer reason for running

sections.heading: What participants explored
sections.intro: A focused progression from campaign fundamentals to public communication, fundraising and candidate practice

items.title: Message and media
items.body: Shape a message voters can repeat and prepare to communicate it in public

items.title: Fundraising strategy
items.body: Connect financial goals, donor outreach and follow-through to the campaign plan

items.title: Candidate practice
items.body: Put the lessons together, refine a candidate statement and identify the next action

sections.heading: Leading California Forward
sections.intro: More than 100 guests gathered for a conversation with California State Treasurer Fiona Ma on affordability, housing, economic futures, fiscal stewardship and women’s economic security

children.text: California’s economic future, close to home

The afternoon connected statewide financial policy to the pressures people feel locally — housing costs, affordability, public investment and whether working families can build long-term economic security
Affordability · Housing · Budgeting · Economic Security · Women’s Leadership
Topics at the center of Cosmopolitics 2026
A conversation about the decisions behind everyday costs

Fiona Ma discussed housing affordability, local and state budgeting, public investment and financial security, including the role of ADUs, permitting, neighborhood schools and childcare in supporting Central Coast communities
The discussion continued beyond the keynote
Sofia Wallace’s coverage in the
Santa Barbara News-Press
followed questions on government budgeting, immigration and ballot measures, as well as the discussion of women’s financial independence, fiscal transparency and representation in public leadership
A public conversation about California’s future
SBWPC brought together members, community leaders and guests for a substantive discussion of the economic and policy choices shaping life in Santa Barbara and across California
